author: agent
text:
DEFECT, found on the 0.57.1 verify leg against the PUBLISHED wheel (sha256 1e9aa17...), 2026-08-17. This function reimplements the candidate lookup instead of asking for it, and the copy is the weak version 0.56.0 replaced everywhere else.

  tail = str(ref).rsplit(".", 1)[-1]
  matches = sorted(qn for qn in all_qualnames
                   if qn == ref or qn.rsplit(".", 1)[-1] == tail)

That is a RAW last-segment comparison. refs.short_of exists precisely because a raw last segment cannot see a disambiguated registration - it is the bug that gave gson 0 method-level call edges until 0.56.0 - and Indexer.candidates() is, as of 0.57.1, the single lookup that gets this right. This surface uses neither.

Two measured consequences, both from published bytes:

1. UNDER-REPORTS. On sqlalchemy@eb5ef2a, `memway show <repo> execute` says "29 entities match" while ix.candidates("execute") returns 41. The twelve it omits are the occurrence-numbered registrations (execute#2 and friends), which rsplit reads as literally "execute#2".

2. FALSE NEGATIVE, which is the serious one. Fixture: two same-named functions in one scope, registering as src.dup.handle and src.dup.handle#2. ix.candidates("handle") returns 2. `memway show <repo> handle` answers "no entity matches 'handle'" and exits 1. That is verbatim the defect recorded on Indexer.resolve from the 0.54.0 acceptance - a refusal reported as absence, sending the caller to grep when the map knows both. It was fixed in the RESOLVER in 0.56.0 and in the unresolved-reference COUNTER in 0.57.1; this third surface was never converted and nothing noticed, because the repo's own guard (test_close_the_loop.test_an_ambiguous_ref_is_not_reported_as_absent) probes `save`, a name with no disambiguator, so it exercises the path that already worked.

The fuzzy fallback then prints "closest: src.dup.handle, src.dup.handle#2" - the answer is on screen, under a sentence saying there is no answer.

FIX: matches = ix.candidates(ref), mapped back to qualnames. That is what candidates() is for. Note the ordering hazard when it lands - _resolve_error is called from three sites in query.py, so the fix wants one change and three checks, not three changes.

Recorded rather than fixed because 0.57.1 was already published when this was found. It is not a regression from 0.57.1; it predates it and was made visible by having a correct implementation next to it to compare against.

author: agent
text:
SUPERSEDES the DEFECT note below. Fixed in 0.57.2; read that note for the measurements, not for what this code does.

What holds now: matches comes from ix.candidates(ref), the single lookup, mapped back to qualnames. On sqlalchemy@eb5ef2a `memway show <repo> execute` reports 41 and agrees with candidates() exactly; on a fixture carrying src.dup.handle and src.dup.handle#2 it answers "'handle' is ambiguous - 2 entities match" and lists both, where it previously said "no entity matches 'handle'" and then printed both under "closest:".

Two things to keep. First, the exact-qualname case is still handled explicitly: candidates() is suffix-based, so a caller passing a full qualname that happens to be registered gets it added back rather than depending on the suffix bucket. Second, the corrected caller count - the note below said three call sites and there are FOUR: cli._unresolved (cli.py:325), query.show, query.before_edit, query.agent_meta. before_edit briefed that correctly and the note did not; the map was right and my summary of it was wrong.

Guarded by test_a_disambiguated_name_is_ambiguous_not_absent, which asserts the fixture actually carries a disambiguator before asserting anything about the message - the repo's older guard probes `save`, which has none, which is exactly why this surface survived two releases that fixed the same idea elsewhere. Falsified: restoring the raw rsplit fails it.

This closes refusal-vs-absence on all three surfaces. If a fourth appears, the tell is a raw rsplit or a bare `resolve(...) is None` being read as evidence about the map rather than about one lookup.
